subject: Week 47: start the whole-milk and bottle-weaning transition plan
bodyText:
This week
Days 327–333: cruising for many and independent steps for some — the CDC walks-alone checkpoint remains 15 months, so pre-birthday walking is a bonus, not the bar. Object permanence is solid, cause-and-effect play is getting deliberate, and gestural communication is rich: pointing, showing, giving, waving. Socially expect warm-with-familiar, wary-with-strangers — which matters for party planning with relatives he sees rarely.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Sleep disruption while visiting family cycles through — hold nap times and the bedtime routine where you can.
- [low concern] Stranger wariness with rarely-seen relatives — normal 10–12-month behavior, not rudeness and not regression.
- [monitor] Sleep regression lasting more than two weeks — bring it to the 12-month visit rather than waiting it out further.
- [call within 24h] Persistent illness in the run-up to party week — resolve it now, not the Friday before.
- [call now] Severe respiratory distress, fever ≥102°F rectal with lethargy, or blue lips or unresponsiveness — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Plan the whole-milk switch: whole cow's milk (not reduced-fat, no toddler formula needed) from 12 months at 16–24 oz per day — more than that crowds out iron-rich food, which is why the 12-month visit checks hemoglobin. Start offering an ounce or two in an open cup at meals now; acceptance often takes 10+ exposures. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/
- Build a cause-and-effect station — pop-up box, ball ramp, drop-a-block chute — and let him run repetitions; deliberate cause-and-effect testing is the cognitive work of this stretch.
- Trade some cruising furniture time for a weighted push toy on flat ground — supported stepping at self-controlled speed, useful whether he walks next week or at 14 months. AAP: Movement 8 to 12 Months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
- Run a daily photo review of party guests — name each relative aloud while he looks; familiar-face pre-loading softens day-of stranger wariness and doubles as labeling practice.

Upcoming
- Day 344–351 (Apr 20–27, 2027): cake and smash-cake order window — custom bakeries want 2–3 weeks of lead for May 11; decide smash cake versus stacked-fruit alternative before ordering.
- Day 364–380 (May 10–26, 2027): 12-month well visit — confirm the booking and start the written question list: sleep, eating range, walking, weaning progress.
- Day 300–365 (Mar 7–May 11, 2027): immersion tour window closes at the birthday — if the L'Academy Nob Hill tour is still unbooked, book it this week.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Stands alone for a few seconds
  AAP window: day 300-365
  What to look for: Often follows cruising. Balance precedes locomotion.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/stands-briefly-no-support/complete

- Uses objects appropriately (cup, phone, book)
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: Functional use — picks up phone and puts it to ear, holds book the right way. Pretend play emerges from here.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-objects-appropriately/complete

- Takes a few steps on her own
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: CDC checkpoint is 15 months. Wide normal range — late walking alone is not concerning if other milestones are on track.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-independent-steps/complete

- Uses one word besides mama or dada
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: Commonly 'ball', 'dog', 'bye', or a family-specific word.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-one-word/complete

- Tries to imitate words you say
  AAP window: day 300-450
  What to look for: Approximations count. 'Wa' for water is a real attempt.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tries-to-imitate-words/complete
